recentItems.title: Israel Election Result: Netanyahu Vs Eisenkot Deadlock, Arab Kingmakers? Many Roads For Bibi, But...
recentItems.description:
Israel has announced its final election results, but the numbers have failed to answer the biggest question: who will actually govern the country? Benjamin Netanyahu's political bloc has emerged as the largest parliamentary force, but it is still short of the majority needed to form a government. His challenger, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has a potential alternative, but bringing together the numbers required to replace Netanyahu could prove equally difficult. And this is where Israel's political deadlock becomes interesting. Now it seems there are five possible ways out of this crisis. Some could bring Netanyahu back into a stronger position, others could give the opposition a chance to take power, and one could send Israelis back to the ballot box. But the biggest surprise is that Netanyahu may not need to win another election to remain politically relevant. The divisions within the opposition could offer him opportunities that the final results do not immediately reveal. So, what are these five possibilities? Why is the opposition struggling despite its combined numbers? And how could Netanyahu turn an electoral setback into another political victory? Watch this video till the end to understand all five scenarios and the political calculations that could determine Israel's next government.

recentItems.title: Russian Jet-Powered Drone Strikes 2 Trains In Dnipro, Cruise Missile Slams Into Ukraine's Chernihiv
recentItems.description:
Officials reported that a Russian drone powered by a jet engine struck two passenger trains at a station in Dnipro, located in central Ukraine, resulting in the deaths of at least 14 people and injuries to 14 others, among them a 40-year-old man who had to have his legs amputated.

In addition, authorities reported that a Russian cruise missile strike in the northern city of Chernihiv took the lives of two 15-year-old girls, while in Kremenchuk, located in central Ukraine, three civilians were killed when a Russian drone struck an apartment block.

The strikes also left 56 people wounded, among them 10 children.
